articles.title: Ex-West Bengal deputy speaker Ashis Banerjee found dead at TMC office
articles.description: Former deputy speaker of West Bengal Assembly, Ashis Banerjee, was found hanging at a TMC party office in Birbhum district on Sunday morning, police sources said. A purported suicide note was also recovered from the party office located near his residence in Hattala Para in Rampurhat, they said. Police reached the spot and sent the body for post-mortem examination. The exact circumstances leading to his death are yet to be ascertained, and police are examining the contents of the purported suicide note, the sources said. Banerjee, a veteran TMC leader, had represented Rampurhat in the state Assembly continuously from 2001 till 2026. He had served as the deputy speaker of the Assembly and held ministerial portfolios, including school education and agriculture, in the Mamata Banerjee government. Tehran says Javad Salehi, Abdolmajid Dashtian and Omran Behraveshian survived and were captured alive by Qatari forces, while a fourth pilot was returned to Iran dead. Iranian officials allege the three have spent months in custody without contact with their families or access for Tehran's representatives. After months of uncertainty over their fate, why is Iran revealing the alleged capture only now?

articles.title: Iran reveals what it pulled from the sky: April 2026 F-15 wreckage on cam, 10 UAVs hit? US shocked
articles.description: Iran has opened an underground IRGC “war trophy” vault filled with wreckage it claims came from U.S. and Israeli aircraft during the 40-day war. Tehran says its integrated air defenses struck 171 aerial vehicles, including 10 manned aircraft. The display features alleged parts from American MQ-9 drones, Israeli Hermes-series UAVs and Starlink-linked communications equipment. Iran also showcased what it claims are remains of a U.S. F-15 destroyed during the April fighting. Tehran is presenting the vault as proof of its wartime success, but do the exhibits substantiate its claims?
